newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stena Line expects to get nod for P&O JV.
newsitem.headline: Stena Line expects to get nod for P&O JV.

text.p: Swedish ferry operator Stena Line said on Thursday it expected a joint venture with Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co (P&O) would be approved by the European Commission and Britain.
"Neither P&O nor us have any indications that it will not go through," Stena Line spokesman Mats Kling told Reuters.
Three authorities have to sanction the proposed joint venture before it can proceed -- the European Commission, the British government and the French government.
The French government on Monday gave its approval to the deal that would merge the two company's ferry operations in the English Channel.
But some uncertainy was caused due to reports that the European Commission's competition service had drafted a "letter of serious doubts" about the deal.
Kling said the fact that France had already given its nod to the merger may help.
"It can not be a negative move," he said.
He said the drafted letter, that has not yet been sent, was "just a technicality".

The final decision to send the letter -- there is a June 11 deadline -- must be taken by European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert in consultation with his transport counterpart Neil Kinnock and the commission's legal service, an EU source said in Brussels.

A spokesman for P&O said UK Trade and Industry secretary Margaret Beckett is expected to publish the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) report on the deal later next week or early the following week.

The deal would create a new company controlled equally by the two groups, but with Stena owning 40 percent and P&O with 60 percent. It would operate the Dover-Calais, Dover-Zeebrugge and Newhaven-Dieppe routes.
